Resampling Schemes for the Bootstrap of a Fit

Source: R/bootstrap_objects.R
resample_method.Rd

Four schemes generate the data sets from which add_bootstrap() refits a model. parametric_resample() draws a new response from the fitted model, case_resample() draws observations with replacement, cluster_resample() draws groups of observations with replacement, and bayesian_resample() gives the observations random positive weights. Each is an object, and the object is passed as the argument resample of add_bootstrap(), bootstrap_vcov() and statmod_bootstrap().

resample_method is the abstract parent of the four classes. It cannot be instantiated, and serves to test membership with S7::S7_inherits().

Usage

resample_method(name = character(0))

Arguments

name

A single string, the short name of the scheme.

Value

Nothing: the class is abstract and its constructor signals an error. Every object that inherits from it has the property name.

Details

The schemes answer two different questions. The parametric scheme simulates from the fitted model, so its replicates have the variance that the model attributes to the estimator, and the bootstrap variance converges to the model-based one (to frequentist_vcov() where the penalties and hyperparameters are held). The case and cluster schemes resample the data, so they do not depend on the variance specification of the model: with a heteroscedastic response fitted by a homoscedastic model the case bootstrap converges to the sandwich variance, which the parametric bootstrap does not. The Bayesian scheme is a smoothed version of the case scheme: its weights are positive, so no replicate loses a level of a factor or separates a logistic regression, and its variance is close to that of the case scheme.

With a kinked penalty (modelterms7::lasso(), modelterms7::enet(), modelterms7::scad(), modelterms7::mcp()) the replicates are those of the penalized estimator. They carry its bias toward zero, so an interval taken from them covers the expected value of that estimator and not the coefficient, and the frequency with which a coordinate is nonzero in the replicates, which summary.StatmodFit() prints, is not the probability that the fit selects that coordinate. Every scheme draws \(n\) observations; resampling fewer than \(n\) is not offered.

A resampled data set is represented by frequency weights, which multiply the weights of the fit. The design is not rebuilt, so the knots of a basis and the levels of a factor stay those of the fit, and a refit on the weights is the refit on the duplicated rows with the basis held. A cluster scheme beside a modelterms7::random() term is the exception: the design is rebuilt on the rows drawn, with the build_info lists of the fit for every term other than the random-effect terms (see cluster_resample()).

See also

parametric_resample(), case_resample(), cluster_resample() and bayesian_resample() for the four schemes, add_bootstrap() for the function that takes one.

Examples

S7::S7_inherits(case_resample(), resample_method)
#> [1] TRUE
try(resample_method(name = "mine"))
#> Error in S7::new_object(S7::S7_object(), name = name) : 
#>   Can't construct an object from abstract class <resample_method>
